proof_nl:
Let x be a real number and m a natural number. By compatibility of coercion with negation, we have (-(m : ℤ) : ℝ) = -((m : ℤ) : ℝ). Also, the natural number m viewed first as an integer and then as a real is the same real number as m viewed directly as a real, so ((m : ℤ) : ℝ) = (m : ℝ). Hence (-(m : ℤ) : ℝ) = -(m : ℝ). Therefore
x + (-(m : ℤ) : ℝ) = x + (-(m : ℝ)).
By the definition of subtraction in ℝ, x - (m : ℝ) = x + (-(m : ℝ)). Thus
x + (-(m : ℤ) : ℝ) = x - (m : ℝ),
as required. Since x and m were arbitrary, the statement holds for all real x and all natural m.
solver_summary: Use that integer-to-real coercion preserves negation, and that subtraction on reals is defined as addition of the additive inverse.
